definition: The reactant that is used up first in a reaction, so it sets the maximum amount of product that can form.
The maximum amount of product that could form, calculated from the limiting reactant and the balanced equation.
The mass or amount of product actually obtained when the reaction is carried out.
The experimental yield divided by the theoretical yield, multiplied by 100.

The molar mass of the desired product as a percentage of the total molar mass of all reactants in the balanced equation; it measures how much of the reactants avoids becoming waste, not how well the reaction worked.
